BRONZE AWAKENING — the great bronze bells heave into their arc, hammers falling in measured thunder, the entire clocktower shuddering alive around each resonant strike.
BRASS PROCESSION — a ranked file of brass automaton-figures rolls forward on polished track, arms raised, eyes lit, the hour counted in their solemn mechanical march.
HAMMER SEQUENCE — each hammer descends in its appointed order, bell after bell ringing outward through the vaulted hall, the air itself trembling with stacked bronze harmonics.
GEAR-HALL SURGE — the strike-train releases and every wheel catches its neighbor, the whole hall erupting into spinning brass, the floor humming under the weight of motion.
PENDULUM CONCERT — pendulum swinging wide, minute-hand lurching forward, bells crying out in unison, steam curling upward as the tower performs its hourly, tremendous confession.
STEAM ERUPTION — pressurized steam blasts through the release valve the instant the hour strikes, wreathing the bell-chamber in white vapor and the smell of hot iron.
CARILLON CASCADE — small bells descend the scale in rippling sequence, each tone chasing the last downward, the cascade filling every stone corridor with shivering, layered music.
CLOCKWORK HERALD — the automaton herald rolls first from the archway, trumpet raised, and behind it the full brass procession follows, wheels clicking, heads turning, marking the hour.
GREAT SWING — the largest bell swings its full tremendous arc, the hammer meeting it with a concussion felt in the chest, the tower rocking faintly in response.
STRIKE-TRAIN RELEASE — the detent drops, the strike-train spins free, and every gear in succession takes the load, the entire mechanism roaring forward like a locomotive leaving station.
SYNCHRONOUS MOTION — pendulum, escapement, strike-train, bells, and automaton-figures all moving at once, the tower a single breathing instrument sounding the hour in perfect mechanical chorus.
VENTING HOUR — as the last preparatory gear clicks into place the steam vents hard, a white column rising past the bells just as the first hammer falls.
PROCESSION OF TWELVE — twelve brass figures emerge in single file for the noon strike, each one bowing as it passes the great bell, the hall luminous with motion.
BELL-HAMMER FALL — the hammer arm pivots on its pin, accelerates, and meets the bell with a crack that sends the tone ringing out across the whole city below.
TURNING HALL — look in any direction and every wheel is moving, the strike-train having released its energy into a thousand gears, the hall alive with synchronized, roaring brass.
RESONANT SURGE — the bronze bell rings and the resonance builds on itself, filling the stone chamber until the walls seem to breathe, the sound enormous and complete.
AUTOMATON SALUTE — each brass figure in the procession raises one articulated arm as the bell tolls overhead, steam wisping from their joints, heads inclined in iron reverence.
CLOCKTOWER BREATH — a long exhalation of steam pours from the pressure release as the mechanism strikes, the tower breathing out through its pipes like a vast, patient engine.
HOUR DECLARED — the minute-hand lurches to twelve, the strike-train drops its count, and the bells answer, swinging and ringing across the rooftops in bright, insistent proclamation.
CASCADING CARILLON — the small bells fire in descending sequence so swiftly the tones overlap, a waterfall of bronze ringing that pours down the tower's interior and floods the street.
MECHANISM ALIVE — every component the eye can find is turning, swinging, or striking, the tower transformed for the duration of the hour-strike into one enormous, purposeful, breathing machine.
IRON THUNDER — the great bell's hammer falls and the sound is less heard than felt, a physical pressure moving through stone and bone, the hour announced as pure force.
BRASS CORTEGE — the automaton-figures process in careful order, gears audible in their chests, glass eyes catching lamplight, the strike-train governing their pace with absolute, clockwork authority.
FULL RELEASE — the stored energy of the weight-driven strike-train pours outward at once, bells ringing, steam venting, figures rolling, every gear engaged, the tower utterly, magnificently alive.
TOWER CHORUS — bells, steam, turning gears, and the rhythmic click of brass feet on the procession-track all sounding together, the clocktower performing its hourly, overwhelming declaration of time.
